headline: TWO OF THE THREE DEFECTS I WAS SENT AT HAD THE WRONG MECHANISM, AND UNDER THE FIRST ONE WAS SOMETHING FAR BIGGER. Defect 1 is real and is now fixed and proved by perturbation — but the line the brief names, `renderer.js:670`, is the ENEMY path, and NPCs never reached `poseFromRig` at all. Chasing that turned up the thing that actually matters: at the Lilmoth player stand, of the **31 NPCs the game draws, 12 were more than 0.15 m UNDERGROUND (worst 2.31 m, i.e. entirely buried) and 15 were more than 0.15 m in the AIR (worst +35.39 m)**. Four of thirty-one were standing on the ground. The authored y is a per-settlement constant — Lilmoth's 54 records carry 0.37, 0.4, 2, 2.68 and 7.37 over ground that is 2.680 — and nothing ever compared it to the terrain. After this round: **0 of 31 buried and 0 of 31 floating**, with the simulation's own numbers untouched. Defect 2's boardwalk-and-clamp explanation is REFUTED by the falsifier r6 itself named: `groundAt(2766, 5011)` = 2.680 and the player's `pos[1]` = 2.680, **gap 0.0000 m**, so the clamp cannot saturate. What is actually hiding the player's feet is the GROUND SKIN, drawn 0.108 m proud of the surface the character is placed on and deliberately excluded from `heightAt` — and `renderer.js` already has `_drawnGroundY()` for exactly this and does not use it for characters. Defect 3 is fixed and its bar is now a measurement of the reference plate rather than an adjective.

defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.the_correction_to_the_brief: `renderer.js:670` is inside `syncEntities`, which iterates `sim.entities` — it poses ENEMIES. NPCs are `syncNPCs`, and its call was `poseStatic(mesh, this._anyRig(sim), n.pos, n.yaw)` — a different function entirely, one that writes no bone and had no ground argument to omit. The r6 pass's CONCLUSION was exactly right (0 of 408 NPCs conformed) and its mechanism was one function off. Both call sites lacked the argument, which is why the conclusion survived the error. Recorded because the next reader will otherwise go to `:670` looking for NPCs and find enemies.
defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.proof_it_did_not_run_before: Perturbation, not inspection. `renderer.groundResolver` swapped for `real + 5.0 m` for one frame, then restored: BEFORE this round the player's `foot_l` moved **0.2493 m** (the clamp, saturated, working) and an NPC's moved **0.0000 m**. A rule with one caller is `RI-MTH07`'s consumption shape and this is its fourth instance this week.
defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.proof_it_runs_now: Same perturbation, same tool, same box: player **0.2493 m**, NPC **5.0000 m**. (5.0 rather than 0.25 because the NPC's whole drawn body now follows the ground and only the per-foot delta is clamped.) And the standing evidence, over all 31 drawn NPCs at both stands: `foot_l` sits between **0.0749 m and 0.0970 m** above its OWN ground, a 22 mm spread around a rest ankle of 0.090 m. Before, every NPC's `foot_l` was at exactly the rest offset with no spread at all.
defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.what_npcs_should_do_on_terrain_and_why: Stand on it. `sim/npc.js:62` takes `pos[1]` verbatim from `post.pos[1]`; enumerated over all 18 files in `game/data/npcs/` (408 records, 346 with a post) the authored y takes ONE OR TWO distinct values per settlement — gideon 2.72; thorn 13.31; stormhold 4 and 141.12; helstrom 6 and 27.22 — so it is a settlement constant applied to people standing in different places and cannot track terrain. The DRAWN character is therefore placed on the ground under it. `n.pos` — what the stealth cones, `world-collision.js` and the sim read — is not touched, which is why the census's `record_delta` column is identical before and after and its `drawn_delta` column went to zero.
defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.what_it_costs: Measured on this box rather than guessed. 60 NPC records are loaded at Lilmoth and 31 have a drawn mesh; the added work is 1 `groundAt` per drawn NPC for the placement plus 2 feet x 5 samples for the conform = **341 calls a frame**. Timing the same call over the whole loaded roster (600 calls) gave **0.96-2.80 ms** across four runs, i.e. ~1.6-4.7 us per call, against a 60 Hz budget of 16.67 ms. It is real and it is affordable; if a future scene loads all 408 it becomes ~4,500 calls and that is a different conversation, which is why the number is written down here.
defect_1_the_conform_that_never_ran.reversal: Delete the three lines that compute `gy`/`drawPos` in `syncNPCs` and drop the `_actorGround()` argument from the three pose calls. Executed on a copy: see `delete_the_fix_control`.

defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.the_r6_hypothesis_is_refuted_by_its_own_: r6 wrote: *'What would falsify it: `groundAt(2766, 5011)` returning within 0.25 m of the player's `pos[1]` of 2.7.'* It returns **2.680**, and the player's `pos[1]` is **2.680**. Gap **0.0000 m**, at both Lilmoth stands, with `body.airborne` false. It is zero BY CONSTRUCTION and not by luck: `engine.teleport` (engine.js:8767) sets `p.pos[1] = this.groundAt(x, z)` and `renderer.groundResolver` (engine.js:543) is that same function, so `gy - groundY` at a standing character is `groundAt(x,z) - groundAt(x,z)`. The clamp never saturates there and the boardwalk plays no part.
defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.what_is_actually_hiding_the_feet: A ray cast straight down at the stand with every actor subtree excluded by object identity finds only two surfaces near the ground: **`ground-skin` at y=2.7879, which is +0.1079 m above the collision ground**, and `ground` at 2.6800. At `street-lilmoth` it is +0.1341 m. There is NO boardwalk mesh at the player stand at all. The player's sole sits at the collision ground plus 2 mm and the whole foot is 88 mm tall, so **the entire foot fits inside the 108 mm by which the drawn ground stands proud of the ground the character is placed on.** The planks in `sheets/04-static-feet-boardwalk-null.png` are the drawn surface, and the legs are not cut off by a deck — they are inside the grass.
defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.and_it_is_deliberate_and_documented: `game/src/world/groundskin.js` says so in its own header: *'The skin is NOT in `field.heightAt()`... this layer changes what you SEE and not what you stand on'*, with the arithmetic reason — Deep Marshes tussocks are 0.34 m of relief at 1.1 m spacing, a 51-degree local gradient, and `traversal.json` refuses ground over 40, so collidng it would fence the province. That decision is right and should not be reversed.
defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.the_fix_exists_in_this_file_already_and_: `renderer.js` carries `_drawnGroundY(x, z, fallbackY)` = `province._meshY() + province._skinLift()`. It was written for W1-13's bloodstain, for precisely this reason, and its own comment names the ground skin. Bloodstains and sapwells consume it. **No character does.** That is the same consumption shape as defect 1, one layer up.
defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.WHY I DID NOT SHIP IT, AND THIS IS THE P: Because the obvious one-liner is a trap and I found the trap before shipping it. `_meshY` reads `f.onDeckAt(x,z) ? f.bareHeightAt(x,z) : f.heightAt(x,z)` — the ground UNDER a bridge rather than the deck — and `renderer.js`'s own comment records that this differs from `heightAt` *'by up to 6.80 m in the Stone Forest and 2.61 m in the Hive'*. Placing characters on `_drawnGroundY` would drop anyone standing on a viaduct into the gorge below it. Trading a 0.108 m defect for a 6.80 m one is not a fix. It also cannot be done as a foot-only conform: on flat ground the drawn-vs-collision difference is UNIFORM, so conforming only the feet lifts both ankles 10.8 cm under a body that has not moved and draws a crouch. The correct change is a whole-body presentation lift with the deck case handled, and that is a piece with its own measurement and its own hardware pass, not a bolt-on at the end of this one.
defect_2_the_player_has_no_feet.it_is_G1's_defect_from_underneath_but_no: `G1-THE-REAL-OCCLUDER-IS-ARCHITECTURE` found the camera inside a deck that is absent from the collision set. This is the same FAMILY — the drawn world and the collided world disagree, and an instrument reading the collided one reports that nothing is wrong — but it is a different dataset and a different direction. G1's is architecture that should be in the collision set and is not. This is a layer that is deliberately out of it, where the presentation is what needs correcting. Fixing G1 does not fix this and vice versa. Saying so is what the brief asked for.

defect_3_the_eye.the_bar_is_now_a_measurement_of_the_plat: `corpus/70-visual/refs/modern/character_closeup/REF-ER__steam-dyules-2764067250.jpg` decoded at native 1920x1080 and sampled with Rec.709 luma over patches: open eye (iris + sclera) mean **63.6**, brightest pixel in that patch **134.9**; cheek below the eye **157.4**; forehead 151.7; nose bridge 153.1. So the eye region is **0.404x the skin around it** and the brightest thing anywhere inside the eye is **0.857x the cheek** — a dark recess with one small light accent, and nothing in the eye brighter than the face.
defect_3_the_eye.a_correction_to_the_r6_description: r6 said the sclera was 'lighter than every humanoid skin swatch'. Recomputed over `RACE_TINT`: 0xa79f8c is luma 159.3 and it is brighter than **5 of the 9** humanoid skins, not all nine — 1.69x a Dunmer (the variant that was photographed, and the worst case) but 0.89x a Nord and 0.84x an Altmer. THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART: one constant cannot be right, because it is a bead on one race and invisible on another. Both eye colours are now fractions of each actor's own resolved skin.
defect_3_the_eye.the_change: sclera = skin x 0.136 linear, iris = skin x 0.712 linear. They are not 0.404 and 0.857 because `THREE.Color.setHex` decodes sRGB into linear working space and `multiplyScalar` scales it THERE, while the plate ratios are of displayed luma — a gamma apart, so the linear scale is ratio^2.2. Setting 0.40 and 0.86 directly measured back as 0.65 and 0.93 and would have left the eye almost as bright as it was; the tool printed that before the numbers were corrected. Roughness also went 0.34 -> 0.62 on the sclera: a tight specular lobe on a sphere is exactly how 'only one of the two catches light' happened, and a recess should read from its value rather than from a highlight that exists at one bearing. Eye and pupil remain separate geometry, as `RI-VIS08` B8 requires; the small bead is now the LIGHT one, which is the plate's structure.
defect_3_the_eye.measured_after: `node tools/visual/f10-r7-eye-contrast.mjs` over all 9 humanoid race tints: recess ratio 0.350-0.394 (bar 0.404), accent ratio 0.847-0.859 (bar 0.857), **0 races with anything in the eye brighter than their own skin**, against 5 of 9 before. The tool reads `RACE_TINT` out of `renderer.js` and the two constants out of `actor.js`, so it cannot drift from the build, and it exits non-zero if any eye ever goes brighter than its face again.
defect_3_the_eye.what_this_does_not_establish: That it LOOKS right. It establishes that the albedo relationship the plate carries now holds on every race. Whether a 0.404x recess reads as an eye or as a hole at conversational distance is a hardware question and it is unanswered.

delete_the_fix_control.result: THE OLD NUMBERS CAME BACK, EXACTLY. Control arm, both stands: as drawn, **12 of 31 buried, worst -2.31 m; 15 of 31 floating, worst +35.39 m** — byte-for-byte the pre-round-7 census. `foot_l` above its own ground spanned **-2.2200 m to +35.4774 m** against the round-7 arm's **0.0749 m to 0.0970 m**. `renderer.js` was then restored from a copy and re-verified by sha256 (`102472ef4fe99348c3492b0bd79f3a589aca7d6a9b31bbc5dd669fdfc8bf7686`).
delete_the_fix_control.and_it_proved_the_specific_claim_rather_: The control arm STILL CONTAINS the whole conform rule — `footConformDelta` and `poseStatic`'s conform block are present in `actor.js` in both arms — and it does nothing at all, because the three call sites are gone. That is the piece's actual claim, isolated: the defect was consumption, not the rule.
delete_the_fix_control.why_this_arm_is_the_right_one: Reverting `renderer.js` alone removes the three CALL SITES while leaving the conform code in `actor.js` present. If the numbers come back to the pre-round-7 values, the change that mattered is the consumption and not the rule — which is the whole claim of this piece.

hazards_worth_recording: A CENSUS THAT READS THE RECORD CANNOT SEE A RENDER-SIDE FIX. My first `after` census reported the same 12 buried and 15 floating as the `before` one, and it was right to: it was reading `sim.npcs[].pos[1]`, which this round deliberately does not touch. The fix is at draw time. The tool now reports BOTH columns, and the record column doubles as the proof that the simulation was left alone. A measurement aimed one layer away from the change reports a null with total confidence.

A RAY CAST FROM ABOVE A CHARACTER HITS THE CHARACTER. The first version of the surface probe reported the top surface at the player stand as y=4.188 on a mesh named `actor-equipment:reed:chest@spine_02` — the player's own chest. Any 'ground under the body' measured without excluding the body is measuring the body. The census now excludes actor subtrees by OBJECT IDENTITY (`playerMesh`, `npcMeshes`, `enemyMeshes` and every descendant), not by name, so a renamed part cannot slip back in.

THE PLACE YOU MEASURE DECIDES WHAT YOU CAN FIND. Four rounds of F10 capture have used the same three stands, and the per-foot ground difference at those stands is bounded at 0.034 m. A conform whose entire mechanism is per-foot height cannot be photographed there, in any number of arms, on any GPU. Two of the last three rounds spent their evidence budget proving that a null was a null. A shot list is a hypothesis about where the thing under test is visible, and nobody had checked this one.

`_drawnGroundY` USES `bareHeightAt` UNDER A DECK. Anyone reaching for it to put characters on the visible ground — which is the obvious and otherwise correct move — will drop every character standing on a viaduct into the gorge, by up to 6.80 m in the Stone Forest. The renderer's own comment carries that number; it is easy to read past it while reading the paragraph for the ground-skin sentence.
